title: HistoryStatusService
responsibility: Reports what Git history proves about one commit: its attached records, their validity and every problem.

inputs.name: HistoryStatusService.constructor.root
inputs.description: Path of the Git repository whose notes, evidence branch and LFS objects are read; it is the working directory of every Git command the service runs. The constructor does not check that the path exists or is a repository.

inputs.name: HistoryStatusService.constructor.pinned
inputs.description: The commits to read history at instead of the live refs: notes is the notes commit, a full 40-character hash or null for no notes, and evidence is the evidence commit whose history bounds which evidence pointers are followed (null follows none). Omitted, the live refs are read.

inputs.name: HistoryStatusService.status.commit
inputs.description: The full 40-character commit hash whose note is read, matched exactly against the keys of all(). A commit with no note, or a hash that matches no key, gives an unverified status with no records and no problems.

inputs.name: HistoryStatusService.problems.line
inputs.description: One verification line from a commit's note: its evidence pointer is loaded, and the record it yields is compared with the line's record id, commit, tree, outcome, base, profile and finish time.

outputs.name: HistoryStatusService.all
outputs.description: Every note of refs/notes/harness, or of the pinned notes commit, keyed by the commit it is for; each ReadNote holds the valid entries written for that commit and the problems of its invalid or foreign lines. The map is read once per service instance and reused by every later call.

outputs.name: HistoryStatusService.verifications
outputs.description: Every verification line of every note, in map order and without de-duplication; reasons, legacy reports and regressions are left out, and an inherited record id is looked up in this list.

outputs.name: HistoryStatusService.status
outputs.description: The verdict for one commit: verified is true only when some record passed and is valid, records holds one entry per distinct record id on its note (the first line for each id), and problems holds the note's own invalid or foreign lines. A commit with no note gives an unverified status with empty records and problems.

problems: manifest does not match the hash in the note
note line 2 is not a valid history entry

outputs.name: HistoryStatusService.problems
outputs.description: The problems with the attached record of one verification line: its own problems (manifest, files, record and identity) when it has any or does not load, and otherwise the problems of the base and referenced records it inherits. Empty when the record is intact and everything it inherits is sound.
examples: manifest does not match the hash in the note

errors.name: ExpectedCliError
errors.description: Thrown with the message 'A notes revision must be a full commit hash.' when the pinned notes revision is neither null nor a full 40-character commit hash, so every read of the notes fails.

errors.name: Error
errors.description: Thrown when a Git command whose output is needed exits non-zero (message 'git <arguments> failed: <stderr>'), when git's batch output does not match the requested evidence blobs ('Invalid Git batch response'), or when an output bound is out of range for an evidence file of about 2 GiB or more ('Command bounds must be positive finite integers.').

errors.name: BoundedCommandFailure
errors.description: Rejected when a Git process the service starts exceeds its time limit (message 'Command timed out after <duration>: git'), exceeds its output limit ('Command output limit exceeded.'), or reports a spawn error.
